## Marico Limited’s Saffola Launches Dual Seed Cold Pressed oils

Combining Saffola’s legacy in heart health, introduces a range of Cold pressed oils both single and dual seed variants

Mumbai, 04 June 2025: Leading FMCG company in India, Marico Limited, has announced its foray into 
the Cold Pressed Oils segment with the launch of the new Saffola Cold Pressed Oils range. Saffola, a 
legacy brand known for its focus on healthy living and heart health, introduces Dual seed Cold Pressed 
Oils—a unique dual-seed format designed to combine the nutritional benefits of thoughtfully paired 
ingredients for everyday cooking. This launch marks a strategic expansion of the Saffola Oils portfolio, 
further strengthening the brand’s commitment to helping Indian households make smarter, heart 
healthy choices in the kitchen. 
With a legacy of over five decades in supporting heart health, Saffola’s entry into the growing Cold 
Pressed Oils category is a natural extension of its expertise. Cold pressed oils are in growing demand 
as they retain the natural flavour, aroma, and nutrients of the seed due to their low-temperature 
extraction process, making them a wholesome addition to everyday meals. By leveraging its 
experience in multi-source edible oils, Saffola brings both single seed and dual seed cold-pressed 
variants to the market, carving a distinct space in this evolving category. 
The new Saffola Cold Pressed Oils range delivers a balanced blend of innovation and authentic taste 
with its Single Seed and Dual Seed options: 
• Dual Seed Cold Pressed Oils: Groundnut & Sesame and Groundnut & Safflower– blended to provide a good fatty acid balance while preserving rich flavour. 
• Single Seed Cold Pressed Oils: 100% Groundnut, 100% Sesame, and 100% Mustard –rich in essential fatty acids, and delivers authentic seed taste. 

Cold-pressed to preserve flavour, the range offers a balanced composition of monounsaturated (MUFA) and polyunsaturated (PUFA) fatty acids supporting everyday cooking that aligns with long term wellness and contains essential nutrients that support cholesterol management

Speaking on the launch, Ashish Goupal, Chief Executive Officer – India Core Business, Marico Limited said, “With the Cold Pressed Oils category gaining momentum in India, we saw an opportunity to introduce a more thoughtful and differentiated offering. At Saffola, we understand the evolving food habits and nutritional priorities of Indian households. This launch of Cold Pressed Oils, allows us to not just participate in the category but to actively shape it. Backed by Saffola’s strong heart-health equity, we are well-positioned to deliver what today’s consumers seek - authenticity, functional benefits, and quality they can trust. This is more than just a portfolio expansion, it’s a step towards building a future where preventive health begins with everyday choices in the kitchen.”

The Saffola Cold Pressed Oils range will be available across India starting at (Rs 356 for 1 litre Mustard, Rs 506 for Groundnut seed and Rs 719 for Sesame), with an initial rollout on quick commerce platforms ensuring convenient access for consumers looking for health-forward cooking oils delivered to their doorstep.

# Marico expands its millets offering with the introduction of Saffola Masala Millets

With this innovation, the company aims to replicate the success of its Oats legacy under the master brand - Saffola

Mumbai, 3rd September 2024: Marico, one of India’s leading FMCG companies, is proud to announce the launch of its latest innovation - Saffola Masala Millets in two new exciting flavours. This new product line capitalizes on the brand’s expertise in democratizing healthy grains, offering a nutritious and flavorful option that aligns with contemporary dietary trends. The new category expands the marque brand Saffola's millet portfolio, reinforcing its commitment to promoting nutritious yet taste-forward ‘better for you’ products.

As an increasing number of new-age consumers seek nutrient dense food options, millets have become a popular choice due to their digestive benefits, natural source of micronutrients, and overall positive impact on health. Addressing the needs of modern Indian consumers, Saffola Masala Millets provides a convenient and delicious ready-to-cook option, encouraging consumer to incorporate millets in their daily life. Thus, supporting the government's vision of encouraging more people to incorporate our very own ‘Sri Anna’ into their daily diets.

Saffola's Masala Millets, rich in fibre and packed with nutritional benefits are available in two flavors beloved by Indian audiences: Masala Delight and Tomato Delight. The unique blend of spices and flavours ensures a satisfying taste experience that appeals to a wide range of palates. This innovation is a testament to Saffola's commitment to providing ‘better for you’ taste-forward products that fit seamlessly into the busy lives of today’s consumers

Speaking on the new launch, Vaibhav Bhanchawat, Chief Operating Officer- India & Foods Business (Marico Ltd.), says, "Building on our Oats No. #1 legacy, we are committed to providing ‘better for you’ taste-forward products, that fit seamlessly into the busy lives of new-age consumers. Saffola Masala Millets is a step towards embracing the nutritious grain with a modern twist of delicious Indian flavours. Our goal is to make wholesome food options accessible and affordable for everyone.” He added “This launch is a part of our broader strategy to expand our millet-based offerings to support the increasing consumer shift towards healthier eating habits. The objective was to create a product that marries the nutritional benefits of millets with the appeal of masala flavors. With Saffola Masala Millets, we aim to pave the way for millets to become a staple in Indian households.”

Saffola Masala Millets come in a convenient 35g pack, priced affordably at just INR 20/-, making them accessible to a wide range of consumers who are seeking Nutritious and tasty food. Saffola Masala Millets are also available on leading Modern Trade chains such as Reliance and Dmart stores.

Empowered by Purpose-led Growth in a Decade of Transformation

In the year under review, your Company’s performance across key parameters was encouraging and reaffirmed Marico’s resilience and clarity of purpose. Despite a complex global environment marked by input cost volatility and geopolitical developments, Marico demonstrated agility and consistency, while remaining focused on long ‑term growth, portfolio transformation, and digital enablement. As we look to the future, our strategic vision remains anchored in delivering sustainable and profitable growth by staying attuned to evolving consumer needs and operating with agility in a dynamic environment. The building blocks of our strategy category leadership, premiumisation, market expansion, and digital enablement, continue to guide our priorities and investments, supported by execution with rigor. We continue to leverage our three core assets, our brands, our talent and our culture, as key enablers of long ‑term value creation. Together, these strengths position us to unlock the next horizon of growth while remaining true to our purpose. FY26 marked an important milestone in Marico’s growth journey, with the Company delivering multi ‑year high consolidated revenue growth, volume growth in the India business and constant ‑currency growth in international markets. As we build on this momentum, we remain sharply focused on our Vision 2030 aspirations, guided by a clear roadmap rooted in innovation, purposeful brand building, and operational excellence.

Innovation & Digital Transformation: Building for the Future

Innovation remains integral to Marico’s growth journey. During FY26, we continued to invest thoughtfully in strengthening our innovation pipeline and focused on addressing changing consumer needs for better efficacy, convenience and holistic wellness. Simultaneously, we accelerated our digital transformation agenda. Data analytics, AI-led insights, and enhanced consumer engagement platforms are increasingly reshaping how we build brands, deepen personalisation and improve speed-to-market. These capabilities are enabling sharper decision-making across marketing, supply chain and demand forecasting. The Marico Innovation Foundation (MIF) continues to serve as a key catalyst in strengthening the innovation ecosystem beyond our balance sheet. Through its flagship Scale ‑Up programme,

Sustainability & ESG: Progress with Purpose

FY26 marked meaningful progress against our ESG 2030 Roadmap, anchored in climate action, circularity, responsible sourcing, people well-being, and robust governance. Our continued commitment to sustainability and responsible business practices is reflected in the strong external recognition we have received across leading global benchmarks. During the year, we made significant progress across our key ESG focus areas, strengthening our commitment to sustainable and responsible growth. In climate action, we achieved an 89.3% reduction in operational GHG emissions intensity (Scope 1 and 2 emissions) against our FY13 baseline, with renewable energy now accounting for 77.3% of our total consumption. I am also proud to share that two of our manufacturing units, Perundurai and Jalgaon, have achieved carbon neutrality.

Our long-term vision remains unchanged: deliver profitable growth, create enduring stakeholder value, and make a meaningful difference to society.

We have achieved 100% operational water footprint offset through robust conservation initiatives, cumulatively generating over 547 crore litres. Water stewardship continues to remain a cornerstone of our sustainability agenda. In responsible sourcing, we continue to deepen engagement with our partners, with 88% of our critical business associates certified at Level 1 and 43% at Level 2, reinforcing our commitment to ethical and sustainable supply chains. Around 92% of our sourcing (by spends) is derived from indigenous sources. As plastic waste continues to rise, the need for scalable recycling solutions and resilient circular systems has become increasingly critical. Our efforts span the value chain – from advancing recyclable packaging solutions to strengthening recovery infrastructure and actively contributing to collaborative platforms such as the India Plastics Pact. Lastly, our strong governance framework remains the foundation of our sustainability journey, with 100% employee certification on our Code of Conduct and 86% of our business associates aligned to our ethical standards. Together, these milestones reflect our belief that sustainability is not a destination, but a continuous journey of improvement, innovation, and accountability.

Innovation continues to be central to our growth strategy. During the year, we introduced several consumer-centric offerings across Foods, Personal Care, Grooming and Wellness. Our approach remains focused on entering adjacent categories where we have a clear right to win, and then scaling them up through disciplined brand building, innovation and execution. In Bangladesh, our shampoo portfolio demonstrates the strength of this playbook, with a strong position built through focused innovation, sustained brand investment and sharp execution. Similarly, in Vietnam, building on our success in Female Personal Care, we further expanded our portfolio with the launch of Body Scrubs and Deodorants. In India, we strengthened the Saffola franchise with a range of cold-pressed oils and continued to innovate across breakfast, snacking and ready-to-cook categories. We also launched Nihar Naturals’ beauty-inspired range of hair oils in three variants - Coconut Rosemary Hair Oil, Coconut Almond Hair Oil and Coconut Aloe Vera Hair Oil. In addition, we expanded the Parachute Advansed premium hair oils range with contemporary ingredient-led offerings such as Olive, Castor and Shea.

As we look ahead, our direction remains clear — Fewer, Bigger, Bolder and Faster. Having nearly doubled our Total Addressable Market (TAM) since FY22, we aim to expand it further to ~3x by FY30 through sharper portfolio choices, accelerated premiumisation and sustained investments in digital and technological capabilities. At a consolidated level, we are poised to deliver double ‑digit revenue CAGR, driven by top ‑quartile volume growth in India and teens constant currency growth in our International business, reinforcing our ambition to deliver H20,000+ Crores in revenues by FY30, while aspiring to achieve a mid ‑teen EBITDA CAGR.

Building on Parachute Advansed’s strong hair care equity, the Protein Shampoo range brings the goodness of coconut milk and natural ingredients into the hair cleansing format. Our digital ‑first model, anchored in data ‑led decision ‑making, rapid innovation, and agile execution, continues to scale up fast, with an emphasis not only on growth but also on improving profitability and capital efficiency. The recent acquisitions are designed to address portfolio white spaces, such as plant-based protein, premium gourmet snacking, and leverage Marico’s distribution and supply chain strengths, and accelerate growth through digital ‑first engagement. We are building our portfolio across three strategic domains: digital foods, digital personal care, and global digital brands, with a clear focus on product ‑market fit, strong unit economics, and long ‑term scalability. SUSTAINABILITY AT MARICO

Reimagining Sustainable Value

Creation for a Transformative Decade

At Marico, materiality is not viewed merely as a reporting requirement; it is a strategic compass that shapes how we anticipate change, strengthen resilience, create long-term value and remain relevant in an increasingly complex and rapidly evolving world.

As global business systems undergo profound transformation driven by climate volatility, technological disruption, geopolitical uncertainty, resource constraints and evolving societal expectations, sustainability considerations are becoming deeply intertwined with enterprise value creation. Increasingly, the organisations that will lead the future are those capable of balancing growth with responsibility, agility with resilience, and innovation with measurable impact. At Marico, we recognise that the coming decade will fundamentally redefine how businesses operate, compete and create value. Our materiality assessment therefore extends beyond identifying present-day priorities; it enables us to evaluate emerging ESG risks, opportunities and systemic megatrends expected to shape the future of the FMCG sector and influence long-term business sustainability.

Our materiality approach is deeply integrated with our ESG 2030 roadmap and serves as a foundational pillar for strategic decision-making, enterprise risk management, governance oversight and stakeholder engagement. It enables us to focus our efforts on the issues that matter most — not only to our business and investors, but also to society, the environment and future generations. Aligned with evolving global frameworks and investor expectations, our assessment incorporates the concept of double materiality by evaluating both: The impact of ESG issues on Marico’s business performance, resilience and long-term value creation; and Marico’s impact on the economy, environment and society through its operations, products and value chain.

Through this lens, sustainability becomes not a parallel agenda, but a core business imperative shaping the future trajectory of Marico.

Materiality in an Era of Global Transition

The sustainability landscape is evolving at an unprecedented pace. Issues once considered peripheral are now central to investor confidence, operational continuity, regulatory preparedness and brand trust. Climate change, biodiversity loss, supply chain disruptions, water insecurity, circular economy transitions and social inequalities are fundamentally reshaping expectations from businesses globally. Simultaneously, capital markets are increasingly integrating ESG performance into investment and stewardship decisions, with heightened focus on:

Climate resilience and transition preparedness Scope 3 emissions and decarbonisation pathways Nature and biodiversity stewardship Human rights due diligence Ethical and traceable supply chains Circular packaging systems Sustainable product innovation Governance transparency and accountability In this evolving landscape, materiality enables Marico to proactively identify strategic priorities, anticipate emerging risks and strengthen long-term resilience in a rapidly changing world.

Further strengthening accountability, key ESG priorities are progressively being integrated into leadership performance evaluation and incentive structures, reinforcing executional rigor and long term commitment towards sustainability outcomes. Strategic Intelligence: ESG Megatrends Redefining Market Competitiveness Our FY26 assessment highlights several structural shifts that will fundamentally redefine the sectoral market landscape and determine sustainable business leadership over the next decade. These trends represent both systemic risks and strategic opportunities for long-term value creation. Climate Transition and Physical Resilience: Navigating the dual challenge of accelerating decarbonization pathways (Transition Risk) while hardening manufacturing and distribution assets against climate induced volatility (Physical Risk). Institutional Investor Scrutiny: The integration of rigorous ESG performance metrics and governance standards into capital allocation decisions, demanding higher levels of non-financial transparency. Nature-Positivity and Biodiversity Integrity: A growing institutional focus on protecting natural capital, requiring the elimination of deforestation from value chains and the restoration of local ecosystems.

Conscious Consumerism and Health-Centric Innovation: Increasing market demand for products that offer superior nutritional profiles, clean labels, and a demonstrably lower environmental footprint. Closed-Loop Systems and Regulatory Evolution: The transition toward a circular economy, catalyzed by stringent international packaging regulations and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) mandates. End-to-End Traceability and Ethical Sourcing: Rising expectations for radical transparency in supply chains, ensuring that every raw material is sourced with integrity and social accountability. Hydrological Security and Resource Stewardship: Mitigating water stress through aggressive replenishment strategies and ensuring resource security for operational continuity in water stressed regions.

Value Chain Human Rights Due Diligence: The institutionalization of human rights due diligence to ensure equality, safety, and fair labour practices across the entire global value chain. Digital Governance and Ethical Technology: Ensuring the responsible deployment of digital tools and AI, focused on data privacy, cybersecurity, and the ethical implications of automation. Standardization of Global Disclosure Frameworks: Navigating an increasingly complex regulatory environment marked by the convergence of global sustainability reporting standards and mandatory compliance requirements. These megatrends are the primary drivers of future business resilience. Proactive integration of these themes into our core strategy will safeguard operational continuity, fortify brand trust, and ensure Marico’s sustained competitiveness in a rapidly evolving global market.

RISK MANAGEMENT

Risk Management as Strategic Enabler

At Marico, we view risk management not as a reactive measure, but as a strategic enabler embedded across all levels of decision-making. Our approach is proactive, integrated, and continuously evolving, ensuring we remain resilient in a dynamic business environment.

As a leading FMCG company operating in a dynamic and highly competitive landscape, we recognize that robust risk management is fundamental to safeguarding our business, sustaining growth, and creating long-term value for stakeholders.

Our Internal Audit function provides independent assurance on the effectiveness of our risk controls while the Risk Management Committee, chaired by the Lead Independent Director oversees the robustness and effectiveness of the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) program.

Risk management is closely aligned with our business strategy and operational objectives. This alignment ensures that key risks are proactively identified, assessed comprehensively, and mitigated effectively.

FY26 reflected the strength and resilience of Marico’s growth model. Core franchises continued to anchor the business, supported by focused premiumisation, wider market participation and robust execution across channels. At the same time, newer growth engines gained salience, driven by more deliberate portfolio choices, sharper resource allocation and sustained investment in high-potential demand spaces aligned to evolving consumer needs. Over the course of the year, we made good progress across our strategic priorities. We continued to strengthen our core franchises and diversify our portfolio. Parachute Coconut Oil delivered resilient performance and further cemented its market leadership. In Saffola Oils, we continued to focus on our premiumisation agenda and expanded our portfolio into cold-pressed oils. The strategy to pivot towards mid and premium segments in Value Added Hair Oils (VAHO) is delivering strong results. Building on the success of shampoos across international geographies, we forayed into the shampoo category in India with the launch of Parachute Advansed Protein Shampoo.

To anchor the next phase of our growth journey towards Vision 2030, our EDGE framework -Expanding TAM & Portfolio, enhancing Distribution & Digitization, Growing Profitably and creating an Empowered Organisation will serve as the backbone for translating our strategic priorities into measurable outcomes.

FY26 marked a year of strong execution and strategic progress for Marico. Against a dynamic and challenging external environment, the Company delivered a robust top-line and bottom-line performance with consolidated revenue growth reaching multi-year highs, reflecting the strength and resilience of our business.

The year was shaped by disciplined and consistent execution by maintaining supply chain agility, navigating inflation through calibrated pricing and cost management, accelerating investments in technology, analytics and automation. At the same time, we continued to strengthen in-market execution and build talent and leadership capabilities for the future.

Most importantly, FY26 demonstrated clear progress against our strategic priorities, reflected in diversification and expansion of our portfolio in India, scale-up of digital-first businesses along with improving profitability, and consistent growth diversification across the international portfolio. As we move towards our journey of Vision 2030, we are building a Marico that is stronger at the core, broader in its growth drivers and more future-ready in its capabilities, guided by our philosophy of 'Fewer, Bigger, Bolder, Faster'.

Our future focused digital-first portfolio is scaling up fast with a clear emphasis on profitable growth. We covered whitespaces of our portfolio in the new age demand segments through strategic investments in Cosmix - a plant-based protein brand, 4700 BC - a premium gourmet snacking brand and Candid in Vietnam - a digital premium skin care brand. Overall, we have made meaningful progress in reshaping our portfolio through organic expansion where our existing portfolio has a strong right to win as well as through strategic investments in the evolving future-need spaces. At the same time, we are progressing towards a leaner and more agile portfolio through sharper choice making. We continue to remain deeply committed to our purpose of ‘making a difference’, by driving sustainable growth, strengthening institutional capabilities, embedding data analytics and AI into decision-making. Sustainability remains integral to this approach, shaping how we operate across brand building, supply chain and community initiatives. Looking ahead, our focus is now on accelerating execution as we move towards Vision 2030. This includes continued focus on strengthening the core, extending in high-growth adjacencies, profitable scale up of digital brands and deepening technological and analytical capabilities. These actions remain central to achieving our next milestones of crossing H15,000 Cr in revenues by FY27 and progressing towards H20,000 Cr by FY30, alongside a mid-teen EBITDA growth aspiration.

Stakeholder engagement forms a critical pillar of our sustainability journey and responsible business conduct. At Marico, we adopt an inclusive, transparent, and agile approach to engagement, enabling us to create enduring value while effectively addressing the expectations of stakeholders who influence or are impacted by our operations. This approach is guided by our commitment to stakeholder capitalism, which shapes how we create shared value across our ecosystem. At its core, this philosophy is anchored in four interconnected principles:

Principle of Governance

Marico’s Stakeholder Engagement framework plays a critical role in shaping its sustainability strategy and governance approach by enabling continuous dialogue with investors, consumers, employees, value-chain partners, communities, regulators, and industry bodies. Insights gathered through these engagements inform the Company’s Double Materiality Assessment (DMA), helping identify and prioritise ESG topics that are material both from a financial impact perspective and from the standpoint of Marico’s impact on society and the environment. The outcomes of this process are further integrated into enterprise risk management systems, ESG target setting under the ESG 2030 Roadmap, policy evolution, and sustainability disclosures across reporting platforms. This stakeholder centric approach enables Marico to proactively address emerging ESG risks and opportunities, strengthen governance mechanisms, and enhance transparency and accountability in disclosures aligned with global and national frameworks. This integrated approach reflects alignment with Global Reporting Initiative GRI 2-29 on stakeholder engagement, SEBI BRSR Principle 4 on responsiveness towards stakeholder interests, and the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, reinforcing Marico’s commitment to inclusive, transparent, and responsible business conduct.

Approach to Stakeholder Engagement

At Marico, stakeholder engagement is embedded as a strategic lever for driving sustainable and inclusive value creation. Our approach is anchored in a structured and insight-led framework that enables us to systematically identify, prioritise, and engage with stakeholders across the value chain. Stakeholder groups are identified through a comprehensive assessment of their alignment with our purpose, as well as their relevance, influence, and proximity to our operations. Based on this evaluation, stakeholders are

mapped and prioritised according to their level of impact on, and interest in, our business. This ensures a focused and meaningful engagement approach. We deploy tailored engagement mechanisms for each stakeholder group, enabling consistent, transparent, and context specific interactions. Insights gathered through these engagements are actively integrated into our decision-making processes shaping our sustainability priorities and guiding ESG interventions in line with stakeholder expectations and our long-term strategy. The process incorporates dynamic materiality considerations, enabling the Company to continuously evaluate evolving impacts, dependencies, risks, and opportunities across the value chain assessed from both financial materiality and impact materiality perspectives in line with emerging global disclosure standards. The rigour of the assessment is further strengthened through structured cross functional participation involving teams across sustainability, risk management, procurement, legal and compliance, human resources, operations, investor relations, and business functions. This enterprise-wide integration ensures that stakeholder insights inform strategic decisions in a cohesive and holistic manner, rather than in functional silos. In addition, Marico incorporates external benchmarking inputs to ensure alignment with evolving global standards and investor expectations.

Criteria and Methodology for Stakeholder Identification

Our stakeholder identification process is guided by the principles of inclusivity, materiality, and responsiveness. Stakeholders are assessed based on their potential to influence, or be influenced by, our business activities, sustainability performance, and value creation journey. This assessment is supported by a structured methodology that evaluates stakeholders across key dimensions such as influence, dependence, strategic importance, and regulatory interface.

The outcome is a prioritised set of stakeholder groups, including consumers, investors and shareholders, employees (including contractual workforce), value chain partners, government and regulatory bodies, and communities. These insights form the foundation of our stakeholder engagement strategy and inform our sustainability disclosures, ensuring alignment with evolving stakeholder expectations and global ESG frameworks. Stakeholders are identified and assessed based on two core dimensions: their influence on Marico’s business decisions and operations, and their dependency on or exposure to the Company’s activities and impacts. This assessment forms the basis of a Stakeholder Prioritisation Matrix that determines the depth, frequency, and mode of engagement for each stakeholder category through channels such as investor interactions, employee forums, supplier assessments, consumer feedback mechanisms, community consultations, regulatory dialogues, independent audits, and grievance redressal platforms. The insights emerging from these engagements are systematically integrated into Marico’s Double Materiality Assessment, wherein sustainability topics are evaluated from both financial materiality and impact materiality perspectives. Topics identified through stakeholder consultations are assessed based on stakeholder significance, business relevance, risk exposure, and strategic importance, resulting in a consolidated Materiality Matrix that defines Marico’s priority ESG themes. The outcomes of this process served as critical inputs in shaping Marico’s ESG Framework and its 2030 roadmap, including the prioritization of strategic focus areas. For more details on Marico's Materiality assessment, please refer to the "Sustainability at Marico" chapter in this Report

At Marico, stakeholder engagement is governed through a robust multi-tiered framework designed to systematically identify, review, escalate, and resolve environmental, social, governance, compliance, operational, and reputational matters with clear accountability across the organisation. The Sustainability Committee chaired by MD & CEO, in alignment with the Risk Management Committee, Audit Committee, and CSR Committee, provides strategic oversight on material stakeholder and ESG issues, including climate-related matters. These are reviewed annually and more frequently when required. The cross-functional Global ESG Council comprising leaders from Marketing, Procurement & Supply Chain, Product Development & Packaging, HR, Finance & Governance,

Manufacturing Operations, and International Business drives execution of the ESG 2030 agenda through dedicated functional taskforces responsible for KPIs, disclosures, and project implementation. Stakeholder concerns and material themes such as climate resilience, sustainable packaging, consumer well being, and ethical supply chains are escalated through defined governance forums to ensure stakeholder perspectives actively shape strategy and decision making. The escalation process follows a defined cascade from operational teams to the ESG Council and Risk Management Committee, and ultimately to the Board for strategically significant concerns, with mitigation actions tracked through continuous monitoring mechanisms. The reporting structure mirrors this governance architecture through

Strategic Oversight and Integration of Stakeholder Perspectives disciplined upward reporting from teams and taskforces to ESG leadership, the Global ESG Council, senior management, and finally the Board Committees. Marico has established a comprehensive, multi-channel grievance redressal framework designed to ensure that every stakeholder from employees and workers to consumers, suppliers, and investors has accessible, transparent, and protected avenues to raise concerns, seek resolution, and hold the organisation accountable. Stakeholders Grievance Mechanism

Grievances are addressed through the Code of Conduct (CoC) Committee, which oversees concerns related to ethics, discrimination, harassment, and human rights. All cases are logged in an internal database management system, investigated by trained committee members, and reported to the CoC Committee for closure. At manufacturing facilities, dedicated Safety Councils and Safety Committees provide an additional site-level avenue for permanent employees and contract workers. Supplementary channels include Business HR connects, townhalls, open house forums, floor connects, skip-level discussions, and periodic pulse surveys conducted via the Glint platform. A formally constituted Internal Committee (IC) receives and investigates complaints under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013. The policy covers all employees, workers, trainees, and business associates. Complaints are investigated promptly and confidentially, with robust protections against retaliation for complainants. From Struggles to Sustainability: A Farmer’s Journey of Transformation

In Kulichettipalayam near Pollachi, Coimbatore, farmer Mr. Ravichandran manages a 10 acre coconut farm with over 600 trees. Like many smallholders, he faced persistent challenges - tree diseases, root infestations, and rising input costs that strained both productivity and profitability. His turning point came when the Parachute Kalpavriksha Foundation (PKF) team, led by Mr. Aravind, visited his farm and conducted a detailed assessment. They identified critical issues and provided practical, science based recommendations: introducing sunn hemp as a cover crop, applying urea and neem cake, painting trunks with calcium hydroxide, and using root feeding treatments to control whitefly infestations. The results were remarkable. Before adopting PKF’s guidance, the farm yielded around 600 coconuts. After implementation, harvests rose dramatically to 8-8.5 loads of coconuts, while soil testing and tailored inputs improved soil health. Input costs reduced substantially, and profitability increased - proving that sustainable practices can drive both productivity and resilience. Beyond technical solutions, PKF’s continuous support made a lasting difference. Mr. Ravichandran received regular field visits, phone guidance, and advice on irrigation practices. With their encouragement, he developed a small farm pond to manage water resources more effectively, ensuring long term sustainability. Today, his farm stands as a model of transformation showcasing how knowledge, innovation, and dedicated support can empower farmers to overcome challenges and thrive. Mr. Ravichandran’s journey reflects the true impact of PKF’s mission: strengthening livelihoods, improving productivity, and building sustainable farming communities.

Mr. Palanisamy, a 65 year old coconut farmer from Coimbatore district, Tamil Nadu, exemplifies how integrated agricultural support can transform livelihoods. Cultivating six acres of coconut, his farm was once plagued by severe pest infestations, declining yields, poor nut weight, and recurring water scarcity. The turning point came when he engaged with the Kalpavriksha initiative under Marico’s Sustainable Agriculture program. Supported by a field service provider (FSP), he gradually adopted improved practices such as mulching, bush cutting, root feeding, drip irrigation, and better fertiliser application. Regular field visits and technical handholding strengthened pest surveillance and nutrient management, while farmer meetings connected him to government schemes and modern techniques. Parallel support from the Jalashay project addressed his most pressing challenge-water scarcity. Construction of a farm pond enabled rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge, ensuring more reliable irrigation across seasons. Within a year, Palanisamy observed significant improvements. Pest incidence dropped, tree vitality improved, and coconut yield and nut quality rose. His income from coconut cultivation increased by nearly 30%, bringing greater financial stability to his household. Enhanced soil moisture retention and consistent irrigation further sustained productivity gains. Digital engagement through the Kalpavriksha mobile app and advisory helpline kept him updated on market prices, fertiliser norms, and government schemes in his local language, strengthening his confidence in independent farm management. Palanisamy’s journey demonstrates how combining scientific farm practices, water infrastructure, and continuous extension support can help smallholder farmers overcome constraints, achieve resilience, and unlock sustainable growth.

Water Brings Hope: Jitendra’s Journey of Renewal

Programme: Water Stewardship: Jalashay

Jitendra and his wife Shital live in Devhari village in Jalgaon district of North Maharashtra. For many years, their main challenge was the lack of water on their 7 acre farm. Their dug well, 50 feet deep and the small naala beside the land were the only sources of water. Every year, Jitendra felt restricted in choosing crops because the water never lasted long enough. Three years ago, Jitendra grew cotton on all 7 acres during Kharif. In the Rabi season, due to limited water, he could cultivate wheat and harbhara on only 2.5 acres, as his well used to dry up by December and the naala by March. Constructing a farm pond was not possible for him due to the financial constraints and land requirement. In 2023, a meeting was called in the village under the Marico’s Jalashay Jalsamruddhi Project. The idea was naala deepening. When Jitendra heard that a bit of land from each farmer would be needed, his family became worried. Giving up land, even a small portion, was not an easy decision. After discussing the long-term benefits, they agreed. Other farmers also supported the activity, and the work was taken up collectively. The well, which dried by December earlier, now had water till the end of February. The naala stayed filled till May. With this confidence, Jitendra changed his cropping pattern. He started cultivating dadar (2.5 acres), jowar (2.5 acres), wheat (2 acres), and brinjal (0.5 acre). From the second crop, he earns around H70,000, which was not possible earlier. His dependence on loans has reduced by almost 60% because of improved yields and lower expenses. He now grows his own fodder, which has further decreased costs. With assured water and fodder, he increased the number of livestock and supplies milk to the dairy, adding a steady income source.

T Transforming Value

Chain Sustainability

At Marico, responsible sourcing is a strategic priority that extends our environmental ambitions beyond the physical boundaries of our owned operations into the complex, multi-tiered ecosystem of suppliers, co-manufacturers, logistics partners, and agricultural value chains that constitute our extended enterprise. SAMYUT our maturity-based responsible sourcing framework is the vehicle through which we operationalise this ambition, building a value chain that is not merely efficient but genuinely accountable, traceable, and aligned with our 2030 sustainability vision.

SAMYUT: Our Responsible Sourcing Architecture

Derived from the Sanskrit word meaning "coming together to achieve," SAMYUT reflects Marico's conviction that sustainability in the value chain is a shared pursuit, not a unilateral demand. The framework is aligned with key international conventions and standards, including the UN Sustainable Development Goals, SA 8000, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and the ILO’s Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work. The Sustainability Committee provides oversight for SAMYUT implementation and integration with procurement practices, ensuring decision-making alignment across our value chain. Purchasing practices towards suppliers are continuously reviewed to ensure alignment with the Code of Conduct and Responsible Sourcing Policy to avoid potential conflicts with ESG requirements. The framework covers all critical value chain partners; suppliers of raw and packaging materials, logistics and transportation partners, warehouse and depot associates, third-party manufacturers, and service providers and is built on three interconnected thrust areas:

Ethical Responsibility Social Commitment Environmental Protection

Legal compliance, anti-corruption, fair competition, data privacy, traceability, human rights, child and forced labour prohibition, diversity and equal opportunity, freedom of association

Employee health and safety, skill development, local community development, land rights of communities in which suppliers operate

Establishment of EMS, emission control, waste minimisation, biodiversity preservation, energy saving, water conservation, and reduction in plastic waste across supplier operations

Applicability of the Samyut Framework

At Marico, the Samyut Responsible Sourcing Framework is integral to our commitment to fostering a transparent, ethical, and sustainable value chain. The framework is applicable to all critical value chain partners, business associates, and approved sub-contractors including suppliers of raw and packaging materials, logistics and transportation partners, warehouse and depot associates, third-party manufacturers, and service providers. Maturity-Based Transition Programme for Critical Supply Chain Partners

To drive continuous improvement and embed sustainability deeper into our supply chain, SAMYUT operates through a structured, three-level maturity pathway ensuring that supplier engagement progresses from awareness through evaluation to active co-creation of sustainability outcomes:

Level 1 – Educate

We initiate supplier engagement by communicating the Samyut requirements and creating awareness around responsible sourcing. Partners are expected to provide formal consent to adhere to the framework and complete a self-assessment of their ESG performance via a structured Level 1 questionnaire.

Level 2 – Evaluate

This phase introduces a comprehensive evaluation mechanism through external audits. The purpose is to validate supplier self-declarations, assess ESG-related risks, and monitor performance across key impact areas. Marico conducts regular performance reviews of critical suppliers under SAMYUT, with defined escalation procedures for non-compliance. The framework enables appropriate action where suppliers are unable to meet minimum ESG expectations within agreed timelines.

Level 3 – Evolve

At this stage, Marico partners with suppliers to implement joint improvement projects, offer technical expertise, and drive measurable improvement in sustainability KPIs. Partners are encouraged to publicly disclose performance metrics aligned with both Marico’s requirements and global sustainability standards. The framework allows for potential supplier support through remote or on-site assistance on corrective and improvement actions as circumstances permit. Marico provides targeted support to suppliers including on-site interventions, improvement action plans, and ongoing ESG capability building/trainings.

Marico's Pursuit of Traceability in Agricultural Sourcing

One of the most significant advancements in FY26 responsible sourcing has been the leap in assessing Traceability of agricultural raw material (by spends) upto location levels from 24% in FY25 to 50% in FY26. This progress reflects the maturation of our strategic partnerships with certified farms, the deployment of technology-enabled traceability tools, and deepened engagement with our SAMYUT framework across agricultural supply chains. Achieving traceability upto location levels for cultivation and/or primary processing, is essential for climate risk assessment and mitigation planning in agricultural value chains, establishing credible deforestation-free sourcing claims, and the long-term integrity of our responsible sourcing program.

Advancing Deforestation-Free Sourcing

Marico is committed to sourcing raw materials in a manner that actively safeguards natural ecosystems and biodiversity. Our deforestation-free sourcing commitments embedded in the SAMYUT framework and the Supplier Code for Responsible Sourcing in agri-based value chains are now backed by substantially stronger operational evidence. We are advancing end-to-end deforestation monitoring through satellite based land-use analytics, supplier declaration protocols aligned with emerging regulatory frameworks (including the EU Deforestation Regulation) and Accountability Framework initiative (AFi), and deepened partnership with suppliers from a biodiversity impact perspective. By strengthening traceability and engaging suppliers on sustainable land-use practices, we are building the supply chain integrity that long term environmental leadership demands. Marico's commitment to nature-positive business is formalised through our Board-endorsed Biodiversity and No Deforestation Policy, which governs our approach across operations and value chains through six structured commitments. We conduct regular ecosystem and biodiversity assessments at all operational sites, applying the mitigation hierarchy avoid, minimise, restore, and offset to ensure no net deforestation across our footprint. Through our SAMYUT responsible sourcing framework, we actively engage suppliers to avoid activities near biodiversity-sensitive areas, while respecting the land rights and traditional knowledge of local communities in our sourcing geographies.

FAST MOVING CONSUMER GOODS (FMCG) SECTOR IN INDIA

India’s consumption landscape continues to undergo a structural transformation, supported by rising disposable incomes, progress in tax and regulatory frameworks, rapid digital adoption, and a broadening aspiration base across both urban and rural markets. Private consumption remains a key driver of economic activity, aided by increasing formalisation and improving access to organised retail and digital platforms. The retail ecosystem is evolving steadily, with a gradual shift in market share from traditional general trade formats towards modern trade, E ‑Commerce, Quick Commerce, and direct ‑to ‑consumer channels. While general trade continues to account for a significant portion of overall retail, emerging channels are gaining traction, reflecting consumer preference for convenience, wider assortment, and faster fulfilment. Digital ‑first and omnichannel models are increasingly influencing how FMCG products are discovered, purchased, and consumed. Premiumisation and formalisation trends continue to strengthen across FMCG categories. Branded products are gaining share, supported by rising quality consciousness, increasing health awareness, and greater willingness among consumers to trade up within categories. New ‑age and digital ‑native brands are scaling-up rapidly by addressing differentiated consumer needs and niche segments through targeted innovation, data ‑driven marketing, and direct consumer engagement. Consumption growth in India is increasingly driven by distinct consumer cohorts. Affluent urban consumers account for a disproportionate share of branded and premium consumption. At the same time, increasing internet and smartphone penetration is helping bridge awareness and access gaps between urban and rural markets, accelerating the adoption of branded FMCG products. Evolving consumption patterns are being shaped by several structural trends, including premiumisation, health and wellness orientation, greater influence of younger cohorts on household spending, rising participation of women in consumption decisions, increased demand for personalisation, and blurring of traditional category boundaries. Together, these factors are reshaping demand across FMCG categories and influencing innovation, pricing, and go ‑to ‑market strategies. For FMCG companies, these shifts are expected to drive further opportunities across core and emerging categories, while also necessitating greater agility in portfolio management, channel strategy, supply chain, cost structures, and consumer engagement models.

This has contributed to faster innovation cycles, increased fragmentation in premium and niche segments, and greater pressure on brand relevance and execution excellence. For established FMCG players, these developments underscore the importance of strengthening digital engagement, accelerating innovation, and enhancing responsiveness across channels to remain competitive in a rapidly evolving market landscape.

Enterprise Risk Management Framework The internal control system is regularly tested and reviewed by Independent Internal Auditor. The independent internal auditor is appointed by the Audit Committee of the Board. All possible measures are taken by the Audit Committee to ensure the objectivity and independence of the Internal Auditor, including quarterly one on one discussions. The Company also has a management audit team which carries out internal control reviews and follow-up audits. The team is also responsible for monitoring implementation of action points arising out of internal audits. There is a robust process to drive adjacencies arising from audit to ensure proactive control across Marico group. The internal auditors and management audit team, as part of their audit process, carry out a systems and process audit to ensure that the ERP and other IT systems used for transaction processing have adequate internal controls embedded to ensure preventive and detective controls. The audit process includes validation of transactions on sample basis to check if the operations of the Company are conducted in compliance to internal policies and ethical standards defined by the Company. The audit report is reviewed by the management for corrective actions and the same is also presented to and reviewed by the Audit Committee of the Board. Internal audits and management reviews are undertaken on a continuous basis, covering various areas across the value chain like procurement, manufacturing, information technology, supply chain, sales, marketing, compliance, and finance with the intent to cover all material business processes and locations under internal audit at least once in every 3-4 years. The internal audit programme is reviewed by the Audit Committee at the beginning of the year to ensure that the coverage of the areas is adequate. Reports of the internal auditors are regularly reviewed by the management and corrective action is initiated to strengthen the controls and enhance the effectiveness of the existing systems. Summaries of the reports and actions taken on audit findings are presented to the Audit Committee of the Board. We have also deployed audit analytics in the domains of sales, procurement, manufacturing, supply chain and employee spends. It helps in continuous control monitoring of control effectiveness and areas where actions are required. The Internal Controls team reviews output of this tool and derives corrective action on timely basis. In order to strengthen control environment, audit analytics will be deployed in other functions of Marico’s India operations as well as key international geographies. Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India, LLP has carried out our internal audit in the year under review. The work of internal auditors is coordinated by an internal team at our end. This combination of our internal team and expertise of a professional firm ensure independence as well as effective value addition and protection.

We have implemented a robust internal financial controls framework within the Company. The Internal Financial Controls have been documented and embedded in the business processes. Design and operating effectiveness of controls are tested by the management annually and later audited by statutory auditors. Statutory auditors have issued an unqualified report after checking the effectiveness of these controls. The management believes that strengthening IFC is a continuous process and therefore it will continue its efforts to make the controls smarter with focus on preventive and automated controls as opposed to mitigating manual controls. The Company has robust ERP and other supplementary IT systems which are integral part of internal control framework. The Company continues to constantly leverage technology in enhancing the internal controls. On a voluntary basis, our material subsidiary, Marico Bangladesh Limited has also adopted this framework. Over time, we will extend this framework to our other overseas subsidiaries.

At Marico, we have always embedded sustainability into our business decisions, allocation of resources, and driving business outcomes. Our focus has always been on strengthening ESG integration as critical input to performance, risk management, and long-term value creation. The past few years, we have enabled strong systems, governance mechanisms, and performance tracking frameworks. In FY26, we have built on this foundation by accelerating execution, shifting from commitment-driven actions to outcome-oriented delivery, with sharper accountability and data-backed decision-making across the organisation. Our ESG 2030 Roadmap continues to provide direction to this transition, supported by a comprehensive set of performance indicators aligned with material sustainability priorities. These indicators are mapped to globally recognised frameworks such as the UN-Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), and SEBI’s Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) requirements. This alignment enables us to remain consistent with evolving regulatory expectations while strengthening the relevance of our disclosures. Building on the 8-point commitment adopted in the past, FY26 saw Marico deepen its efforts across these strategic pillars. Our focus remained steadfast on delivering measurable progress across Net Zero in manufacturing operations, enabling circular economy, scaling responsible sourcing practices, advancing inclusion and diversity, safeguarding human rights, and embedding ethical conduct across the value chain. These commitments continued to guide our actions, supported by robust governance mechanisms.

This principle encompasses all practices and policies that promote equality, dignity, and well-being of the workforce who are involved in a company’s value chain or within its own organization, without discrimination and in a way that respects diversity, as well as the provision of decent work for all of them.

This principle emphasises that companies should put safety and resource efficiency first when designing and producing their goods. The goods must be produced in such a way that, from the time of their conception until their final disposal, they minimize and mitigate their negative effects on the environment and society while also adding value. This principle pushes organizations to comprehend all material sustainability challenges throughout the life cycle and value chain of their products.

This principle aims to adopt, implement, and make disclosures about company’s ethical conduct and transparency in business operations. The principle emphasizes the use of ethical business practices across the value chain of the company and is put into practice using the company governance structure by defining economic, social, and environmental responsibilities.

This principle acknowledges that businesses should recognize that they operate within a broader ecosystem of stakeholders, including shareholders, investors, communities, and the environment. They are responsible for understanding and managing the impacts of their products, operations, and business practices, with a focus on enhancing positive outcomes and preventing, minimizing, and mitigating adverse effects on stakeholders, natural resources, habitats, and society at large.

This principle acknowledges that business functions are under national and international regulatory and policy frameworks that direct their growth and give distinct limits and bounds. The idea acknowledges that corporations can legitimately interact with governments to have their complaints heard or to have their opinions heard in the formulation of public policy. Additionally, public policy advocacy must advance the common good according to the law.

According to this principle, a company’s main goal is to provide safe products and services to its customers, thereby generating value for both. Acknowledging that consumers have several options for products and services, businesses work hard to offer products that are secure, reasonably priced, simple to use and safe to discard. Businesses, together with other important stakeholders, play a pivotal role in reducing the negative impacts of excessive consumption of their products on the society’s overall well-being.

The principle highlights the national and development agenda in accordance with the goals and priorities of the government, while identifying the country’s social and economic development difficulties. This is important in areas where social unrest and low human development are prevalent. This principle encourages commercial, governmental and civil society collaboration. This idea affirms the interdependence of economic success, inclusive growth and equitable development.

A brief on types of customers Marico is one of India’s leading consumer products companies in the global beauty and wellness space. It operates in product categories such as Coconut Oil, Refined Edible Oils, Value Added Hair Oils, Leave-in Hair Conditioners, Male Grooming and Packaged Foods, among others. Marico’s product portfolio caters to a diverse range of consumer needs and preferences, ranging from hair nourishment and styling to nutrition, immunity, and healthy snacking. Marico has a large distribution network of more than 10,200 distributors and stockists covering over 5.8 million retail outlets across urban and rural India as well as strong presence across key Modern Trade chains and E-Commerce platforms. This network helps us reach out to more than 60,000 villages in India and almost every Indian town with population over 5,000. The backbone of the well-connected distribution channel which ensures availability of our products to consumers are the state-of-the-art facilities which includes 6 manufacturing facilities, 25 warehouses and 4 re-distribution centres.

5. Specific commitments, goals and targets set by the entity with defined timelines, if any.

Marico’s sustainability journey reflects a progressive shift from a compliance-driven approach to a 
deeply integrated ESG-led business strategy, embedded across its operations and value chain. The 
journey began with the identification of 5 core focus areas in FY17: climate change, water, responsible 
sourcing, circular economy, and social commitments under which Phase 1 targets were successfully 
achieved by FY22. As the sustainability landscape evolved and stakeholder expectations deepened, 
Marico reassessed its approach to set more ambitious and future-focused goals. This led to the launch 
of the Marico’s ESG 2030 Roadmap on the 50th anniversary of World Environment Day (5 June 
2022), marking a renewed commitment towards the Decade of Action leading up to 2030. At Marico, 
sustainability is underpinned by a structured materiality assessment to prioritise ESG topics most 
relevant to the business and stakeholders. In FY25, we conducted a Double Materiality Assessment 
evaluating both enterprise value impacts, societal and environmental impacts, aligned with CSRD 
principles and global frameworks including GRI 2021, SASB, and the S&P Global CSA. 
Building on this strong foundation, the framework is now structured around 8 key focus areas that 
drive Marico’s strategic ESG priorities. 
1. Climate Change: Achieve net-zero emissions across Indian manufacturing operations by 
2030 and global operations (owned-manufacturing units) by 2040; streamline decarbonization 
initiatives across business ecosystem to reduce overall carbon footprint. 
2. Water Stewardship: Become a ‘water steward’ organization by creating water availability for 
community and ensure water neutral operations.

Marico has instituted a multi-tiered governance framework to steer its Business Responsibility policies, ensuring strategic oversight, effective implementation, and accountability across levels. The Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer (“MD & CEO”) holds the highest level of accountability for the implementation and oversight of Marico’s Business Responsibility policies. As the Chair of the Sustainability Committee, the MD & CEO is supported by a core group of senior executives (CXOs), ensuring that the principles and commitments outlined in these policies are effectively embedded across the organisation’s operations and decision-making processes. The Committee is responsible for monitoring progress against defined sustainability objectives, overseeing the management of emerging risks and opportunities including those related to climate change, regulatory developments, and stakeholder expectations and ensuring alignment with the company’s strategic vision. The Committee may meet at such periodicity as it deems fit to discuss the aforesaid matters. The Committee also ensures that the Business Responsibility policies are operationalised with integrity, periodically reviewed for relevance, and transparently communicated to all stakeholders, including shareholders, regulators, and the wider public. At the executive level, the Global ESG Council drives cross-functional execution and achievement of targets, while dedicated sustainability teams ensure on-ground implementation and monitoring.

EI-3.Describe the processes in place to safely reclaim your products for reusing, recycling, and disposing at the 
end of life, for (a) Plastics (including packaging) (b) E-waste (c) Hazardous waste and (d) other waste. 
Marico operates in the food and cosmetics sector, with products intended for end-consumer use. As such, product reclamation 
is not performed, and post-consumption packaging materials sometimes enter municipal waste streams. To address this, Marico 
runs an Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) program. Within our supply chain, we have established processes to retrieve 
expired, damaged, or leaked items, ensuring their disposal or recycling is managed in an environmentally responsible manner. 
Our facilities and value chains are supported by a robust waste management system that ensures accurate accounting of all types 
of waste. We also require that all waste management vendors are approved by the Central and State Pollution Control Boards, in 
strict compliance with regulatory procedures.

b. What are the processes used to identify work related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine basis by the entity? Marico is committed to adopting industry-leading safety practices at every stage to identify workplace hazards and evaluate risks associated with both routine and non-routine activities. For routine operations, methodologies such as Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA), Job Safety Analysis, Hazard and Operability Studies (HAZOP), along with internal and external audits, are effectively employed to minimize risk exposure across operational areas. For non-routine tasks, risks are primarily managed through a structured work permit system. In addition, specific guidelines and procedures are established to uphold project safety standards during infrastructure modifications. A robust Management of Change (MOC) process further supports risk assessment and ensures that appropriate precautions are implemented during execution.

EI-10. Health and safety management system a. Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the entity? (Yes/ No). If yes, the coverage such system? Yes. Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) management is deeply embedded across all functions at Marico. A robust system is in place at every manufacturing site, office, and operational location to monitor both leading and lagging OHS indicators. The digitalization of the safety management system has enabled stakeholders to complete tasks efficiently and on time. Furthermore, all Marico-owned manufacturing facilities are certified under ISO 45001:2018. Recognizing health and safety vulnerabilities within our supply chain, we have extended OHS systems to depots and third-party manufacturers as well. Each location has a designated individual responsible for driving OHS initiatives. Monthly reviews are conducted to assess emergency preparedness and proactive risk mitigation. In addition, external agencies are engaged to provide an added layer of due diligence, strengthening health and safety practices at depots and third-party manufacturing units.

LI-6.Provide details of any corrective actions taken or underway to address significant risks / concerns arising from assessments of health and safety practices and working conditions of value chain partners. As part of Marico’s responsible sourcing initiative, SAMYUT, value chain partners, including material suppliers, warehousing providers, and converters are systematically assessed by internal teams as well as accredited external agencies. These evaluations cover critical parameters such as labour practices, occupational health and safety, environmental compliance, and overall operational standards. The Company adopts a structured and proactive approach in addressing identified gaps through the implementation of corrective and improvement action plans, including on-site interventions and ongoing ESG capability building wherever required. A robust Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) framework is deployed under supplier quality and responsible sourcing programs to ensure timely remediation and prevent recurrence of issues. Marico further strengthens supplier performance through targeted training, awareness initiatives, and capacity-building programs, enabling alignment with its health, safety, and human rights standards. Continuous monitoring through periodic internal and external audits ensures early identification and mitigation of potential risks across the value chain. During FY26, we continued to prioritise risk-based supplier evaluation, with 43% of suppliers (by spend) assessed and supported through tailored corrective action plans to strengthen sustainability and compliance performance across labour and human rights, health and safety, and environmental management. In FY26, Marico facilitated site visits and third-party assessments, supporting partners in implementing corrective actions. These interventions focused on enhancing process design and strengthening safety measures, with particular emphasis on reducing operational risks, improving electrical safety, reinforcing emergency preparedness, and advancing work-zone monitoring practices.

Stakeholder consultation is integral to Marico’s strategy for identifying and addressing key environmental and social challenges. Demonstrating its commitment to inclusive and responsible growth, Marico has established its ESG 2030 Roadmap, built on a robust and evolving Materiality Model that aligns with its core purpose of creating meaningful impact for both people and the planet. Each stakeholder group is aligned with a unique key proposition, a guiding principle that shapes Marico’s approach to building long-term, meaningful relationships. This model emphasizes proactive engagement and is supported by over 50 key performance indicators (KPIs), which are monitored and disclosed on an annual basis. The feedback and insights obtained through this structured stakeholder engagement process, are systematically integrated into the company’s policies and operations, ensuring that stakeholder expectations are closely aligned with Marico’s strategic priorities. As a result of this ongoing dialogue, Marico has defined an 8-point commitment focused on delivering measurable outcomes in critical areas such as climate change, water stewardship, responsible sourcing, sustainable agriculture and farmer livelihoods, inclusion and diversity, and corporate governance.

Aligned with this approach, Marico is focused on enabling its value chain partners to build resilient, future-ready, and sustainable businesses. At the same time, the company is integrating ESG-driven objectives into its talent acquisition, capability building, and employee engagement initiatives nurturing a strong ESG-first culture across its broader ecosystem. As per the classification, marginal farmers are those with landholdings below 1 hectare, while small farmers are those with landholdings between 1–2 hectares. In FY26, PKF enrolled 22,798 farmers under the program (2.05 Lakh cumulatively enrolled), of which 19,881 farmers (~87%) belong to the small and marginal farmer category. Considering the socio-economic vulnerabilities associated with smaller land holdings, these farmers have been identified as marginalized stakeholders. Based on their identified needs, the Parachute Kalpavriksha Foundation (PKF) team is currently implementing focused interventions and strategic community development initiatives aimed at supporting and benefiting these communities.

Marico has institutionalized a comprehensive and well structured grievance redressal framework to effectively address concerns pertaining to violations of the Code of Conduct, Human Rights issues, discrimination, harassment, and matters governed under the POSH (Prevention of Sexual Harassment) Policy (https://sustainability.marico. com/uploads/1692583938967-marico-posh-policy-pdf. pdf) The framework is supported by clearly articulated procedures, periodic awareness and sensitisation programs, and a robust reporting mechanism that facilitates timely, transparent, and accessible reporting of incidents. EI-9.Do human rights requirements form part of your business agreements and contracts? (Yes/No) Marico embeds human rights requirements within its business agreements and contractual arrangements through its comprehensive Code of Conduct for Business Associates (https://sustainability.marico.com/ uploads/1757502740534-code-of-conduct-for-business associates-pdf.pdf), which serves as a mandatory framework governing all third-party relationships. This Code is applicable to a wide spectrum of business associates including suppliers, vendors, contractors, and service providers and establishes clear expectations on ethical conduct, labour standards, and human rights compliance. The Code explicitly mandates adherence to social accountability principles, including the prohibition of child labour, forced labour, slavery, and human trafficking, thereby reinforcing Marico’s commitment to fundamental human rights. It requires business associates to ensure a non-discriminatory and inclusive work environment, promoting diversity and equal opportunity while prohibiting discrimination across multiple parameters. Provisions on maintaining a harassment-free workplace further strengthen safeguards related to dignity and respect at work. Extensive coverage of parameters such as fair wages, working conditions, freedom of association, and employee health & safety, ensuring alignment with internationally recognised human rights and labour standards. Establishment of proper grievance redressal mechanisms within the operating ecosystems of business associates, to address employee concerns related to legal violations or breaches of these principles. The Code is endorsed by the Board of Directors and is enforced through contractual obligations, with violations potentially leading to disciplinary action, including termination of the business relationship.

Describe the strategy adopted by your company to reduce usage of hazardous and toxic chemicals in your products and processes and the practices adopted to manage such wastes. Marico has institutionalized a comprehensive and structured waste management framework across its establishments, guided by the principles of reduction, reuse, recycling, and responsible disposal, in alignment with its environmental sustainability commitments. Waste generated across operations is segregated at source into hazardous and non-hazardous streams, with robust tracking mechanisms and record-keeping practices to ensure traceability and regulatory compliance. The Company conducts periodic waste audits and maintains detailed data monitoring systems to identify reduction opportunities and drive continuous improvement. A substantial share of waste is recycled or reused, with a significant proportion diverted away from landfills through authorised recycling and co-processing channels. All waste disposal is carried out through authorised and certified vendors, following strict due diligence and adherence to applicable environmental regulations and pollution control norms. Marico is advancing towards its ambition of Zero Hazardous Waste to Landfill, reflecting its commitment to circularity and responsible waste management. Two of our manufacturing units, Perundurai and Puducherry respectively have been certified by TUV SUD South Asia Private Limited as verified Zero Waste to Landfill (ZWL) facilities. In addition, Marico implements its Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) obligations for plastic packaging in compliance with regulatory requirements. Through this, the Company ensures the collection, recycling, and environmentally sound disposal of post-consumer plastic waste, working with authorised recyclers and partners to strengthen circular economy outcomes. Marico has implemented the "SAMYUT" responsible sourcing initiative, which integrates labour practices, ethics, health and environmental concerns, and safety across the value chain. Three stages of maturity are included into the program: At the outset, all suppliers are required to undergo a mandatory certification program on Marico’s Code of Conduct for Business Ethics. Alongside this, the first level of Samyut certification, Level 1, involves self-assessment of ESG practices aligned with Marico’s responsible sourcing principles, while Level 2 involves thorough evaluation by third party to assess the overall management of all environmental, social and ethical parameters as per the Marico Samyut framework, within the suppliers’ operations. In FY26, critical value chain partners with a business share of more than 88% have completed Level 1 certification, while a business share of more than 43% have completed Level 2 certification. This includes raw material and packaging material suppliers as well as dedicated third party manufacturers.

The internal Crisis Management Committee plays a vital role in developing crisis response strategies, communication protocols, and overseeing regular training and capability building initiatives. Marico encourages consumers to follow healthy lifestyle and good cooking practice through campaigns like World Heart Day. In 2025-26, Saffola Heart to Heart Talk initiative was launched. Designed to encourage people to pause and reflect on their daily habits, the brand

campaign underscored how small, routine behaviours can shape long-term heart health outcomes, especially among young Indians. Through the initiative, Saffola engaged consumers in a simple yet personal conversation about their movement, sleep, eating patterns, and overall lifestyle. The AI-enabled experience categorized respondents into indicative heart health zones, revealing that while many individuals demonstrate positive intent towards their well being, a significant number still show signs that point to the need for greater consistency in adopting heart-healthy habits. At the same time, the initiative nudged participants to think more deeply about the quality and balance of their everyday food choices at home, including cooking practices and ingredient selection. By using AI to mirror real-life habits, we aimed to make heart health conversations simpler, more relatable and actionable. Your Company believes that Risk Management is an integral and important aspect of Corporate Governance. It is a strategic enabler embedded across all levels of decision-making and is closely aligned with the Company’s business strategy and operational objectives. A robust Risk Management Framework ensures adequate controls and monitoring mechanisms for smooth and efficient running of the business. Regular risk assessments, scenario planning and stress testing are conducted to evaluate preparedness and refine the Company’s response strategies. Your Company believes that robust risk management is cornerstone of protecting and maximising shareholder value. Your Company implemented the ERM 2.0 framework to stay ahead of the curve and become risk intelligent. The ERM 2.0 framework continues to guide the Company’s risk management approach, enabling proactive identification, assessment and mitigation of risks. The key cornerstones of your Company’s Risk Management Framework are: ❖ A well-defined risk management policy; ❖ Structured Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Program; ❖ Periodic assessment and prioritisation of risks that affect the business of your Company; ❖ Development and deployment of risk mitigation plans to reduce vulnerability to prioritised risks; ❖ Focus on both the results and efforts required to mitigate the risks; ❖ Defined review and monitoring mechanism wherein the functional teams, senior management, Risk Management Committee (“RMC”), Audit Committee and the Board review the progress of the mitigation plans; ❖ Comprehensive ERM Framework; ❖ Integration of Risk Management with strategic business plan, annual operating plans, performance management system and significant business decisions; ❖ Constant scanning of external environment for new and emerging risks; ❖ Wherever applicable and feasible, defining the risk appetite and implementing adequate internal controls to ensure that the limits are adhered to.
